intro: Estavayer-le-Lac is a medieval lakeside town in the canton of Fribourg, on the south shore of Lake Neuchatel. On a terrace above the water in the old town stands a very old large-leaved lime that local accounts date to the 1470s, with a view across to the lake. It is on public ground in the old town, above the lake shore, and free to see.

location.address: Place de Moudon, Estavayer-le-Lac, Fribourg, Switzerland

trees.story:
On a terrace above Lake Neuchatel in Estavayer-le-Lac, a lime has grown into something that hardly looks like a single tree. The trunk has split and healed around its own hollows, and several stems have twisted round each other into a cluster of ridges and knots. Roots grip the gravel like fingers.

Its age rests on tradition. A publication of the canton of Fribourg puts its planting around 1474, and local legend links it to the Battle of Morat in 1476. A tourist guide gives only the sixteenth century. Either way the tree is some four and a half to five and a half centuries old, and nobody has counted rings.

The photograph shows the lime in full leaf at the edge of the terrace, with a stone wall, a bench and a window box of pink geraniums beside it, and the lake and hills behind. The upper limbs spread out of a trunk that looks too small for them, held up by the thick roots of its base.

It stands in the open on public ground, so no ticket or permission is needed.
trees.how_to_recognise: A massive, hollow, many-stemmed lime on a terrace with a low stone wall and a bench, looking out over Lake Neuchatel.
